title: Temperature-Dependent Electron Thermal Transport Governs Atomistic Mechanism of Femtosecond Laser Ablation of Inconel 718
content: Femtosecond-laser processing of nickel-based superalloys is limited by incomplete knowledge of how energy deposited in the electron gas is converted into atomic motion within the first tens of picoseconds. Here we establish a two-temperature molecular-dynamics model of Inconel 718 in which the electron thermal conductivity is not frozen at its ambient value but keeps its intrinsic temperature dependence, so that the instantaneous electron diffusivity collapses while the lattice is hot and recovers as it cools. The dependence is implemented by re-instantiating the solver in 27 segments and passing the electron-temperature field from one segment to the next, which reproduces the intrinsic dependence without fitting parameters. The model closes the energy balance to within −6.8% to +4.0%, and its predictions for the surface temperature history, the melt-depth scaling, the amplitude and decay of the laser-induced stress wave, and the surface phase constitution are then tested against independently reported femtosecond-ablation data for the same alloy. Replacing the constant diffusivity by the temperature-dependent one raises the 40 ps surface temperature of the 220 mJ cm⁻² case from 2 374 K to 3 216 K, which removes an 18% under-prediction of the reported temperature at 40 ps and leaves an 11% overshoot, lowers the peak melt depth from 68.2 nm to 50.6 nm, and increases the peak compressive stress by 5.9%; the residual discrepancies share a single origin. The ablation mechanism is then resolved at the atomic level: an electron-phonon non-equilibrium window of 0.4–1.9 ps, melting within 0.5 ps, a cooling stage controlled by resolidification at 77–245 K ps⁻¹, and a fluence-dependent transition from the face-centred cubic lattice to a disordered state that proceeds inward behind the melt front. The results provide the physical basis for fluence-resolved, atomically precise shaping of Inconel 718.
